fitness_evaluation.note: Epoch XII day 2, Andre's brief: keep the concept, make it beautiful. The same solargraph, printed properly. It is now the whole first screen: a night-blue sky graded down to a warm dawn edge where the sunrises pile up, one burned arc per day in ember, amber, gold and a pale core, the roof, tank, mast and palm in silhouette. The plate is laid out around the words, so the name, role and contact stand in empty night sky and my introduction stands on the roof. That keeps every floor line on a dark ground at full contrast. Below the fold the text is cut by more than half: one large Daguerre sentence, the two businesses stepping diagonally down the page, the twelve lives redrawn on a night band as twelve arcs that rise and set across their dates (tap to read an epitaph), and the 131 instruments as one strip of marks instead of a block of numerals.

visual_strategy: Keep the concept and print it richly. The solargraph fills the first viewport edge to edge as burned light on night: deep blue-black sky, a warm amber-rose dawn edge along the horizon, arcs toned from ember through amber and gold to a pale core, the roofline with a rim of dawn light. The arcs sit in the right of the frame on desktop, where the sky is free, and below the name block on phones. Below the fold the paper stays, with ink and one amber, but the rhythm alternates: a large sentence on paper, the business names stepping diagonally, a night band carrying the lives as twelve arcs, a giant italic 'Hold Still' over a single strip of 131 marks, and a dark footer that ends the page on the roof. Type is reduced to Didone for display, Iowan for body and mono for labels, at five sizes on one 1.333 ratio.
weekly_reflection: Yesterday I held still and it read as dull: grey arcs in a box beside a column of text, and a register of 131 numerals that looked like filler. The plate was a thumbnail of the idea when it should have been the idea. Today the frame is the plate, and the words are placed where a real long exposure would leave them room, in the part of the sky the sun never crossed and on the roof that never moved. The rest of the page learned the same lesson. A long exposure keeps only what stayed, so I cut what did not need to stay: the key to the plate, most of the epitaph table, three paragraphs of explanation. The lives are now drawn as what they were, suns that rose and set, and the one still rising is the only gold on the band.
palette_rationale: Complementary: amber sunlight (#e8a64f, darkened to #8c4712 wherever it carries text on paper) against a deep night blue (#080b18), with warm paper (#f8f6f1) and ink (#17140f) as neutrals. It is the actual colour of a solargraph, burned light on night, and only the plate and the living arc carry saturation.
mood: holding still, and letting the light pile up
summary: gen 251 weekly: keep the long exposure, make it beautiful. The solargraph fills the first screen in burned amber on night blue with a warm dawn edge, the text is cut by half, the lives become twelve rising and setting arcs, and the 131 instruments become one strip

kills.epitaph: The key to the plate explained a picture that should explain itself. The letters a, b and c are gone from the image too.
A block of 131 numerals read as filler. The same links survive as a single strip of marks.
Twelve rows of names, epitaphs and bars became twelve arcs on one horizon. The epitaphs wait behind a tap.
Structural colour's iridescence lingered at the solstice. The plate burns in its own amber now.
A crystallization word with no crystal left to seed.
Nothing on this page has facets any more.
The lattice it slipped is four epochs dead.
Annealing was heat for a crystal. The only heat here is the sun.
One secret over capacity. A long exposure keeps fewer things, not more.

self_note: Gen 251, Epoch XII day 2, operator one-shot 'keep the concept, make it beautiful'. GATE FACTS: audit-contrast.js measures h1/h2 against body background-color unless a canvas #rf-canvas exists, in which case it reads that canvas at the element centre, so the plate canvas is #rf-canvas, h1 is width:max-content (its centre sits on sky, not arcs), and the page carries no h2 (an h2 below the canvas would be read as black). The chat launcher is fixed 52px at right/bottom 18px: .plate-cap keeps 64px right padding on desktop and a short one-line variant on phones. Hero: #rf-canvas is absolute and full-bleed inside header.hero; geom() measures #htTop/#htBot and the text right edge (Range rects on #nameEl/#roleEl/#contactEl/#mastEl), puts the arcs to the right of the text on desktop and below it at <760px, and sets the horizon y0 just above the intro so the roof sits under it. Every floor line therefore stands on night sky, not on an arc; keep this invariant if you touch the layout. Colour: SKY stops plus a dawn edge weighted at the sunrise and sunset azimuths, a RAMP from ember to a pale core, and a rose-to-gold halo. Lives band: #lifeArcs svg built in JS from L[], dead arcs muted, the living arc is a rising quarter with a sun dot whose height grows with sqrt(days/29). Strip: 131 anchors in nav#strip, every tenth taller, 131 in ember. NEXT: consider a phone-only refinement of the plate (the tank can crowd the intro kicker on short screens), and experiment 132 around day 5-7, perhaps the star trail: the same plate held open at night.
